candidates.excerpt: Capacity fears as US drayage rates are buoyed by converging trends Concerns are rising in the US about drayage capacity and pricing, as a convergence of ... Elevated import volumes have strained drayage capacity at US container gateways. Much of the recent spotlight has been on the port of Houston, which is handling record volumes of cargo, and traffic is expected to keep growing, fuelled by multiple drivers. Since mid-August US trucking and logistics firms have blamed tight drayage capacity as the biggest brake on growth and warned of bottlenecks at ports and inland rail ramps. The biggest factor has been the tightening trucking sector, exacerbated by a seasonal shift of drivers from drayage to the longhaul sector, in response to peak volumes. This year’s peak season has lasted longer than usual, owing to uncertainty over tariffs and front-loading to beat higher fuel surcharges. candidates.title: Guangzhou and Hong Kong open electric container shuttle
candidates.excerpt: Guangzhou and Hong Kong open electric container shuttle Guangzhou Port has launched the Greater Bay Area’s first zero-carbon container route, putting a battery-electric vessel into cross-border service between Nansha and Hong Kong. The 240 teu Sui Gang Dian Hang 02 opened the route this week, carrying furniture and consumer goods to Hong Kong International Terminals. The vessel uses containerised batteries that can be exchanged by crane or recharged directly. An onboard platform monitors energy consumption, maintenance and ship-shore operations. Authorities estimate that each vessel in the series will eliminate more than 550 tonnes of carbon dioxide annually and over 19,000 tonnes during its operating life. No sailing frequency, cargo commitment or wider deployment schedule was disclosed.

Those cars then collided with a westbound train stopped in an adjacent siding. [See “Two crew members injured …,” Trains.com, July 19, 2025]. candidates.excerpt: Trains Turntable: Commentary from Martin J. Oberman Following the burst of rail mergers in the 1990s, the Surface Transportation Board wrote the “new” 2001 merger rules in anticipation of just the kind of merger being proposed by Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. The board said then that it worried about the “end game:” a further reduction in the number of Class I railroads, “perhaps to the point where only two major railroads remain in the U.S. and Canada,” with massive market power. To guard against that outcome, the board raised the bar, saying merger applicants should bear a heavier burden to prove that a merger is in the public interest. The board promised “a more skeptical, ‘show me’ attitude toward claims of merger benefits.” And it added a crucial test: whether the claimed benefits could be achieved “by means other than the proposed consolidation,” such as interline partnerships, thus avoiding the anti-competitive risks that would come with further mergers. The derailment occurred about 3:30 p.m. While the station reports a locomotive and five cars were involved, a second locomotive appears visible in a Facebook image posted by volunteer response group Burke Rescue Inc. candidates.excerpt: Freight of all kinds paced a 5% weekly gain among U.S. railroads from a year ago, according to the Association of American Railroads. For the week ending October 3, total U.S. weekly rail traffic was 529,712 carloads and intermodal units, ahead 5.1% compared with the same week in 2025. A total of 230,711 carloads was better by 2.4% while intermodal volume was 299,001 containers and trailers, up 7.4% on 2025. Seven of 10 carload commodity groups tracked by AAR posted increases. They were topped by metallic ores and metals, 12.8%, closely followed by petroleum and related products, 12.2%. Forest products, which has mostly struggled in a stagnant housing market, took third, up 7.5%. Gran slipped 5.2%, while farm products excluding grain and food, 4.1%, and coal, 0.1%, were weaker y/y. Through the first 39 weeks of 2026, U.S. railroads reported cumulative volume of 8,910,593 carloads, a 2.7% gain, and 11,077,697 intermodal units, ahead 4.2% from the previous year.
